data.body: Decisions that a future run should not re-derive. (a) Per-ticket last-synced timestamp REJECTED on measured evidence: it is mechanically a revert of ADR 0060 section A1, whose 12.79KB->1.74KB measurement was taken on that exact field; ~69 of 72 daily passes currently produce zero bridge-state commits because every writer is change-guarded, and an always-written timestamp inverts that (~180x churn). updated_at cannot stand in for 'last synced' - 908 of 1914 entries are byte-identical to created_at. (b) 'bridge status' needs no new producer: last-run time is derivable three independent ways that agree; only the health record needs redirecting to a durable path. (c) The pause mechanism is inverted today - the portable, remote-persisted ref-lock gate has no writer while the GitHub-specific 'gh workflow disable' is the wired path, which is the portability violation driving the bridge epic. (d) 'jira' rejected as the noun (other trackers planned); 'bridge' approved; 'reconcile' retired without an alias. (e) The 800-LOC cap acts as an attractor - 11 of 24 cap-crowding files fall into the 200-500 target band once comments are triaged, but event_append.py, _processors.py and signing.py cannot be fixed that way (replay-compat and security invariants).
